block.summary: The block at a position, as a value that compares and prints as its name.
params: the position, as `[x, y, z]` or as three loose arguments
or the name of a block, to build the value without reading the world
block.returns: `block` — printed and compared it is its name, `'minecraft:stone'`.
examples: block.block('oak_stairs[facing=north]');        // from a name, with properties

block_state.summary: The properties of the block as a map, or the value of one of them.
params: optional: the name of a single property
block_state.returns: `map` of name to value, or the single value; `null` when the property is not there.

block_data.summary: The NBT of the block entity - the content of a chest, the text of a sign.
block_data.returns: `nbt` — the data, `null` when that block has no block entity.

block_tags.summary: The tags the block belongs to, or whether it belongs to one of them.
params: the position of the block, or a block value
block_tags.returns: `list` of tags, or `bool` when a tag is given.

block_list.summary: Every block the game knows, or the ones carrying a tag.
params: optional: only the blocks of that tag

solid.summary: Whether the block is solid - something you can stand on and cannot walk through.
examples: if(block.solid([x, y - 1, z]), print('there is ground here'));

air.summary: Whether there is air at that point.

liquid.summary: Whether the block is a liquid - water, lava, or something modded that behaves like one.

flammable.summary: Whether fire can catch on that block.

transparent.summary: Whether the block lets light through.
transparent.returns: `bool` — whether it is transparent to light.

blocks_movement.summary: Whether the block stops whoever walks into it.

suffocates.summary: Whether the block suffocates whoever ends up inside it.

hardness.summary: How hard the block is to break.
hardness.returns: `num` — the hardness; `-1` when it cannot be broken, as for bedrock.

blast_resistance.summary: How well the block resists explosions.

block_sound.summary: The sound group of the block, the one deciding the noise of steps and breaking.
block_sound.returns: `str` — the name of the group, as `'stone'` or `'wood'`.

map_colour.summary: The colour the block shows on a map.
map_colour.returns: `str` — the name of the colour on the map.

ticks_randomly.summary: Whether the block gets random ticks - the ones growing crops and spreading grass.

power.summary: The redstone signal the block emits.

light.summary: The total light at that point, whatever it comes from.

block_light.summary: The light coming from blocks - torches, lava, glowstone.

sky_light.summary: The light coming from the sky, before the time of day is taken into account.

effective_light.summary: The light that really counts for spawning: the sky one lowered by the time of day.
effective_light.note: It is this one, not `light`, that answers "can something spawn here at night".

emitted_light.summary: The light the block itself gives off.

see_sky.summary: Whether that point has open sky above it.

brightness.summary: The brightness at that point as a number between zero and one, the way the game renders it.

set.summary: Places a block, with its properties.
params: the name of the block, or a block value taken from the world
the properties, as pairs or as a single map
set.returns: `block` — the block placed, `null` when nothing changed.
examples:
// copying a block along with its data
block.set(there, block.block(here));
set.note: A property the block does not have is an error, with the right name suggested — not a silent default.

destroy.summary: Breaks the block: with drops, without, or as if a given tool had broken it.
params: `-1` for no drops, or an item such as `'diamond_pickaxe'`; with `[name, count, nbt]` its enchantments count

harvest.summary: Breaks a block the way that player would break it, with their tool and enchantments.
harvest.note: Unlike `destroy`, it fires the events and the statistics of a real breaking: it counts for the tool durability and for whoever is listening.

place_item.summary: Uses an item on a block, the way a player clicking on it would.
params: the item to use, as a name or a triple
optional: whether to respect the placement rules of the game
place_item.returns: `bool` — whether the use had an effect.

update.summary: Forces a block update at that point, as if a neighbour had changed.
examples:
// after a bulk build inside without_updates
for(edges, block.update(_));

block_tick.summary: Runs the scheduled tick of the block right away.
examples: block.block_tick(water_pos);   // makes the water flow one step

random_tick.summary: Gives the block one random tick, the kind that grows crops.

without_updates.summary: Runs an expression without letting block updates spread.
params: what to run, usually a build
without_updates.note: Nothing is updated when it ends either: call `update` on the edges if the build has to settle.

signatures: create_explosion(pos, power, type, fire, source, cause)
create_explosion.summary: Sets off an explosion at a point.
params: optional: the strength, `4` like TNT by default
optional: the entity to blame for the damage

pos.summary: The position of an entity, with its decimals.
examples: block.set(block.pos(player), 'stone');   // it floors on its own

pos_offset.summary: A position shifted in a direction.
params: optional: how many blocks, one by default
examples:
// the block a face is pointing at, inside an event
block.pos_offset(clicked, face);
